items.label: text
items.text: Some materials(such asmetals)are good electrical conductors.Other materials that do not allow electricity to flow through them easily areknown as insulators.

items.label: text
items.text: Allatoms contain small particlescalled protons,neutrons and electrons.The protons arefound in the centre ornucleusof the atom and carry arelative charge of+1.The neutrons are also in thenucleus of the atom but carry no charge.The electrons travel around the nucleus in orbits.The electrons carrya relative charge of-1.

items.text: Figure 9.2A neutral atom has the same number of negative electrons and positive protons (not to scale).

items.label: text
items.text: Normally the numberofprotons in the nucleus isequal to thenumber of orbiting electrons.The atom therefore has no overall charge.Itis neutral.Ifan atom gainsextra electrons,itis then negatively charged.lfan atom loses electrons,it becomespositively charged.Anatom thatbecomes charged by gainingorlosingelectronsiscalled anion.

items.label: text
items.text: It ispossible tocharge some objects simplybyrubbing them together.But these objectsmustbemade from differentmaterialsandthesematerialsmust be electrical insulators,

items.label: text
items.text: We can test which materials are conductors andwhich are insulatorsusing the circuit in Figure 9.3.

items.label: text
items.text: Ifweplacea conductorbetween A and B thebulbwill shine.lf we place an insulatorbetweenAand B the bulbwill not shine.

items.label: text
items.text: Materials such asgraphite andmetals such as copper,tin and gold allow electricity to flow through them easily.They are electrical conductors.

items.label: text
items.text: Materials such asplastic,rubber,glass and wood donot allow electricity to flow through them easily.They are electrical insulators.
